recommendation: Keep the audit commit as-is. No core follow-up is needed for FHIR-26961 unless a future work group decision changes the extension-pack context or asks for different Appointment insurance guidance.
issue_request: The Applied PA issue asked whether the request-insurance standard extension should apply to Appointment. The final Not Persuasive with Modification resolution rejected adding that extension context because it was not well-defined enough for real-world Appointment coverage details, and instead directed the spec to remove request-insurance from core use and add Appointment narrative guidance for expected coverages and prior authorization.
initial_application: Core commit 45e03786be5a7a1f907ce67d4b534f36b42357e5, "FHIR-26961 Insurance and appointments guidance", added the Insurance for Appointments and Payment Authorization for Appointments sections to source/appointment/appointment-notes.xml. Current core source only retains the historical request-insurance OID outside generated history and has no active core request-insurance StructureDefinition or extension page reference.
additional_context: FHIR-26526 started the broader request-related extension review and spawned the Appointment insurance follow-up. FHIR-I minutes first sent the question back to PA, PA minutes record the later Not Persuasive with Modification direction to remove the extension and add notes, and the FHIR Extension Pack now carries request-insurance for NutritionOrder and CarePlan without Appointment as a context.
reconciliation: Published an empty no-change audit commit. No source edit was made because the active Appointment resource is build-scoped, the current Appointment notes already contain the approved guidance, Appointment.account is available as the Account reference relied on by the resolution, and the remaining request-insurance definition is outside core and does not enable Appointment.
